revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Festival Tickets
revealWordProblem.text:
Four friends are doing yard work around town to earn money for the Summer Music Festival advertised on the flyer. Tickets are $75.50 each. They charge $15 per hour for yard work and will combine their earnings.
Question: How many hours do the four friends need to work to earn enough money to buy four tickets? Propose a breakdown of how many hours each friend might work.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A Summer Music Festival flyer for August 5th and 6th at River Park Arena, priced at $75.50 per ticket.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Four tickets cost 4 × $75.50 = $302. At $15 an hour, write the inequality 15h ≥ 302, so h ≥ 302 ÷ 15 ≈ 20.13 hours. They cannot work part of an hour and come up short, so together they need at least 21 hours — which earns 21 × $15 = $315, enough with $13 left over. Split evenly that is 21 ÷ 4 = 5.25 hours each, so a workable breakdown is three friends working 5 hours and one working 6 hours.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents: 'The temperature is less than 40 degrees'?
questions.explanation: 'Less than' means <, so the inequality is t < 40.
choiceFeedback: Your symbol opens toward temperatures ABOVE 40. 'Less than 40' lives on the other side — which way should the symbol point?
The ≤ symbol lets the temperature be exactly 40. 'Less than 40' leaves 40 out.
An equals sign pins the temperature to a single value, but this situation describes a whole range of temperatures.
hints: Find the comparison phrase: 'less than 40 degrees'. Does 40 itself count, or only temperatures below it?
'Less than' with no 'or equal to' means a strict symbol — no bar underneath — pointing toward the smaller side.
Test a value: is 35 degrees 'less than 40'? Yes — so pick the strict symbol that puts t on the smaller side of 40.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'La temperatura es menor que 40 grados'?
questions.explanationEs: 'Menor que' significa <, así que la desigualdad es t < 40.
hintsEs: Halla la frase de comparación: 'menos de 40 grados'. ¿Cuenta el 40 mismo o solo las temperaturas por debajo?
'Menos que' sin 'o igual a' significa un símbolo estricto —sin barra debajo— apuntando hacia el lado menor.
Prueba un valor: ¿35 grados es 'menos de 40'? Sí, así que elige el símbolo estricto que pone t del lado menor de 40.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents: 'You must be at least 48 inches tall to ride'?
questions.explanation: 'At least' means greater than or equal to, so h ≥ 48.
choiceFeedback: So close — test the boundary. Does a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall get to ride? Your strict symbol turns that rider away.
This describes riders who are too short to ride. Check which direction the symbol opens.
This would let anyone shorter than 48 inches ride. 'At least 48' makes 48 the smallest allowed height, not the largest.
hints: 'At least 48' — ask yourself: can a rider who is EXACTLY 48 inches tall ride? That decides whether 48 is included.
When the boundary value is allowed, you need a symbol with the 'or equal to' bar under it.
Allowed heights are 48, 49, 50, and up. Pick the symbol that includes 48 itself AND points toward bigger numbers.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Debes medir al menos 48 pulgadas de estatura para subir'?
questions.explanationEs: 'Al menos' significa mayor que o igual a, así que h ≥ 48.
hintsEs: 'Al menos 48': pregúntate si alguien que mide EXACTAMENTE 48 pulgadas puede subir. Eso decide si el 48 se incluye.
Cuando el valor del límite sí se permite, necesitas un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual a' debajo.
Las estaturas permitidas son 48, 49, 50 y más. Elige el símbolo que incluya el 48 Y apunte hacia los números mayores.

questions.stem: Which inequality represents: 'A store can hold no more than 75 people'?
questions.explanation: 'No more than' means less than or equal to, so p ≤ 75.
choiceFeedback: Almost — check the boundary. Is a store holding EXACTLY 75 people breaking the rule? Your symbol says yes; re-read 'no more than.'
This says the store always holds 75 or more people, which is the opposite of a limit. 'No more than' caps the number.
This describes crowds larger than the limit. 'No more than 75' means the store never goes above 75.
hints: 'No more than 75' — could the store hold exactly 75 people? Could it hold 76?
'No more than' allows the boundary but nothing above it — that calls for a symbol with the 'or equal' bar.
Test values: 75 people is fine, 76 is not. Pick the symbol that keeps p at 75 or below.
questions.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'Una tienda puede albergar no más de 75 personas'?
questions.explanationEs: 'No más de' significa menor que o igual a, así que p ≤ 75.
hintsEs: 'No más de 75': ¿podría la tienda tener exactamente 75 personas? ¿Podría tener 76?
'No más de' permite el límite pero nada por encima: eso pide un símbolo con la barra de 'o igual'.
Prueba valores: 75 personas está bien, 76 no. Elige el símbolo que mantenga p en 75 o menos.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Write Inequalities is using a strict symbol (> or <) for a phrase that actually includes the boundary value. For 'the suspect is at least 18 years old,' students often write a > 18 instead of the correct a ≥ 18 — this wrongly excludes 18 itself, even though 'at least 18' means 18 counts as a match. The same error happens in reverse with 'at most': for 'the getaway bag holds at most 12 items,' students write n < 12 instead of n ≤ 12. Always ask: does the key phrase include the number ('at least,' 'at most,' 'no more than,' 'no fewer than' → use ≥ or ≤) or exclude it ('more than,' 'fewer than' → use > or <)?

level1.stem: Which inequality represents: 'The speed limit is more than 25 mph'?
level1.explanation: 'More than' means strictly greater than, so s > 25.
choiceFeedback: Test the boundary value: is 25 itself 'more than 25'? Your symbol includes it — decide whether the words allow that.
The symbol points the wrong way. 'More than' describes speeds above 25, not below it.
An equals sign names one exact speed, but 'more than 25' covers every speed above 25.
hints: 'More than 25' — is exactly 25 included, or only speeds above 25?
'More than' (not 'at least') is strict — no 'or equal' bar under the symbol.
Test: 26 works, but 25 itself does not. Pick the strict symbol that puts s above 25.
level1.stemEs: ¿Qué desigualdad representa: 'El límite de velocidad es más de 25 mph'?
level1.explanationEs: 'Más de' significa estrictamente mayor que, así que s > 25.
hintsEs: 'Más de 25': ¿se incluye exactamente 25 o solo las velocidades por encima de 25?
'Más de' (no 'al menos') es estricto: sin barra de 'o igual' debajo del símbolo.
Prueba: 26 sirve, pero 25 no. Elige el símbolo estricto que pone s por encima de 25.

level2.stem: A parking garage charges if your stay is more than 2 hours. Which inequality represents times t that are charged?
level2.explanation: 'More than 2 hours' means strictly greater than: t > 2. Exactly 2 hours is not charged.
choiceFeedback: Think about the driver who stays exactly 2 hours. Your symbol charges them — does 'more than 2 hours' include exactly 2?
This describes short stays, which are not charged. Check which side of 2 the symbol opens toward.
This would charge a stay of exactly 2 hours, and it also covers shorter stays. 'More than 2' leaves 2 out and looks above it.
hints: The charge starts once the stay goes PAST 2 hours. Is a stay of exactly 2 hours charged?
If exactly 2 hours is NOT charged, the boundary is excluded — that rules out any symbol with the 'or equal' bar.
Test t = 2 and t = 3: only stays longer than 2 are charged. Pick the symbol that makes t = 3 true but t = 2 false.
level2.stemEs: Un estacionamiento cobra si tu estancia dura más de 2 horas. ¿Qué desigualdad representa los tiempos t que se cobran?
level2.explanationEs: 'Más de 2 horas' significa estrictamente mayor que: t > 2. Exactamente 2 horas no se cobra.
hintsEs: El cobro empieza cuando la estancia PASA de 2 horas. ¿Se cobra una estancia de exactamente 2 horas?
Si exactamente 2 horas NO se cobra, el límite queda excluido: eso descarta cualquier símbolo con la barra de 'o igual'.
Prueba t = 2 y t = 3: solo se cobran las estancias mayores de 2. Elige el símbolo que haga verdadero t = 3 y falso t = 2.

level2.stem: A clue says the suspect carried at least 12 stolen gems. Which inequality shows the number g of gems?
level2.explanation: 'At least 12' includes 12 and any number above it, so g ≥ 12.
choiceFeedback: 'At least' includes 12 itself, so the symbol must allow equal to as well as greater than.
This allows fewer than 12 gems. 'At least 12' makes 12 the smallest possible number, not the largest.
This rules out 12 itself along with everything above it. 'At least' points the other way and includes the boundary.
level2.stemEs: Una pista dice que el sospechoso llevaba al menos 12 gemas robadas. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra el número g de gemas?
level2.explanationEs: 'Al menos 12' incluye el 12 y cualquier número mayor, así que g ≥ 12.
hints: An inequality has two things to decide: which direction it points, and whether the boundary number is included.
'At least 12' means 12 itself is allowed, so the symbol needs an 'or equal to' part.
Start with the boundary: 12 counts. Now decide whether the gem count goes above 12 or below it, and pick the matching symbol.
hintsEs: Una desigualdad tiene dos cosas que decidir: hacia dónde apunta y si el número del límite se incluye.
'Al menos 12' significa que el 12 sí se permite, así que el símbolo necesita la parte 'o igual a'.
Empieza con el límite: el 12 cuenta. Ahora decide si el número de gemas sube por encima de 12 o baja, y elige el símbolo que corresponde.

level2.stem: A witness reports that fewer than 5 people entered the building. Which inequality shows the number n of people?
level2.explanation: 'Fewer than 5' does not include 5, so n < 5.
choiceFeedback: 'Fewer than 5' does not include 5 itself, so equal to should not be allowed.
The symbol points the wrong way. 'Fewer than 5' describes counts below 5.
This includes 5 and everything above it. 'Fewer than 5' excludes 5 entirely.
level2.stemEs: Un testigo informa que menos de 5 personas entraron al edificio. ¿Qué desigualdad muestra el número n de personas?
level2.explanationEs: 'Menos de 5' no incluye el 5, así que n < 5.
hints: Decide two things: which way the inequality points, and whether 5 itself counts.
'Fewer than' excludes the boundary number, so no 'or equal to' part is needed.
5 is not allowed and the count has to stay below it. Write the symbol that says exactly that.
hintsEs: Decide dos cosas: hacia dónde apunta la desigualdad y si el 5 mismo cuenta.
'Menos de' excluye el número del límite, así que no hace falta la parte 'o igual a'.
El 5 no se permite y la cantidad debe quedarse por debajo. Escribe el símbolo que dice exactamente eso.

level2.prompt: Write two different real-world situations: one that uses > and one that uses ≥. Explain why the situations need different symbols even though both mean 'bigger.'
level2.sentenceFrame: Situation 1 (>): ___. This uses > because ___. Situation 2 (≥): ___. This uses ≥ because ___. The difference is that ≥ includes ___ while > does not.
level2.hint: Use a strategy or example from the lesson to help you explain your answer.
hints: The whole difference between > and ≥ is the boundary number itself: one includes it, one leaves it out.
Pick real rules: 'score more than 10 points to win' (strict) versus 'you must be at least 13 to watch' (boundary counts). Explain each choice.
Write situation 1 with 'more than' and test its boundary number — it should fail. Write situation 2 with 'at least' and test — the boundary should pass.
level2.explanation: The only difference between > and ≥ is whether the boundary number itself is allowed. A rule like "score more than 10 points to win" leaves 10 out, so it needs >, while "you must be at least 13 to watch" lets exactly 13 count, so it needs ≥. Testing the boundary number in your own situation is the quickest way to check which symbol fits.
level2.explanationEs: La única diferencia entre > y ≥ es si el número del límite está permitido. Una regla como "anota más de 10 puntos para ganar" deja fuera el 10, así que necesita >, mientras que "debes tener al menos 13 años para verla" permite exactamente 13, así que necesita ≥. Probar el número del límite en tu propia situación es la manera más rápida de saber cuál símbolo va.
level2.promptEs: Escribe dos situaciones diferentes de la vida real: una que use > y otra que use ≥. Explica por qué las situaciones necesitan símbolos distintos aunque las dos signifiquen 'más grande'.
hintsEs: Toda la diferencia entre > y ≥ está en el número del límite: uno lo incluye y el otro lo deja fuera.
Escoge reglas reales: 'anotar más de 10 puntos para ganar' (estricto) frente a 'debes tener al menos 13 años para verlo' (el límite cuenta). Explica cada elección.
Escribe la situación 1 con 'más de' y prueba su número límite: debe fallar. Escribe la situación 2 con 'al menos' y prueba: el límite debe pasar.
